subject: Fleet reserve & runway proposal for BrightPath renewal
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:18:00Z
Subject: Renewal planning: capacity safety pool ask

Sergio,

Thanks for the quick sync today. Per our forecasting team, Q4 inference volume is trending ~48% above the renewal baseline we originally committed to — driven by a new multimodal feature set and a marketing burst. Attached is our Q3 export (brightpath_q3_usage_report.csv) with token-level peaks by hour.

Short ask: BrightPath would like Redwood to provision a temporary safety pool (hot standby) that covers an expected 6–8 week surge window during the renewal period. Rough numbers: we estimate needing the equivalent of ~40 H100 GPUs for steady surge capacity, plus an operational hot-standby buffer of ~10% to cover model warmup and KV cache priming.

We want to avoid a lengthy tranche negotiation if Redwood can present a short, staged plan that:
- preserves SLA and p99 latency targets,
- minimizes one-time provisioning overhead, and
- includes a rollback if peak demand subsides.

Can your team propose a runway + reserve that maps to our usage curve and includes measurable rollback triggers? Procurement is on copy for the renewal timeline.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Infrastructure, BrightPath AI
--- Attachment: brightpath_q3_usage_report.csv (CSV, 2.4 MB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity safety pool ask

Liam — thanks for the data and the context. This is the kind of signal we need to avoid underprovisioning during a renewal window. I looped in Kimberly to run a quick sizing pass and Ben / Vanessa for operational impact.

High-level response: yes, we can present a staged reserve that meets your constraints. Two quick design principles we'll validate internally and share as a proposal:
1) Staged tranches: start with a scaled-in reserve (~25 GPUs) to cover the first 2 weeks, then auto-scale to the full surge size (~40 GPUs) if a rolling 7-day median crosses your projected threshold.
2) Thermal headroom (hot standby): we recommend a 10–12% hot-standby lane dedicated to quick-start requests so KV cache priming doesn't harm p99 latency for primary traffic.

Kimberly — can you run a utilization sensitivity for BrightPath's hourly peak and add an ops-impact note (scheduling, prewarming cost, expected incremental egress)? Ben/Vanessa — can you model reserve routing and what this looks like in Dedicated vs. a short-term Dedicated burst on Hosted?

I'll consolidate and share a PDF draft (redwood_proposed_reserve_v1.pdf) by EOD.

Thanks,
Sergio
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: redwood_proposed_reserve_v1.pdf (draft, 480 KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity safety pool ask (sizing pass)

Team — quick sizing notes after running BrightPath's CSV through the utilization engine (attached in my internal notes):

Observations:
- Peak hourly token rate aligns with needing ~38–44 H100-equivalent GPUs for sustained peak 60–90 minute windows.
- Median utilization across Q3 is ~62%; spikes hit 88–93% for short bursts.

Proposed runway (numbers):
- Phase 0 (default): reserve +10 GPUs over baseline for a 7-day trial (cost-effective, low-risk).
- Phase 1 (triggered): if 7-day rolling median > 70% for CPU-equivalent token load, scale to +30 GPUs for next 14 days.
- Phase 2 (surge): if sustained 3-day peak > 85% and business confirms burst marketing window, scale to +40 GPUs with a 12% hot standby lane (i.e., 5 GPUs held in warm state).

Operational considerations:
- Prewarm cost estimate: ~0.6x hourly of H100 per warm GPU for the priming window (30–90 minutes).
- Rollback triggers: 14-day rolling median < 55% => automatically ringdown tranche by 50%; 28-day rolling median < 50% => remove reserve.
- Observability hooks: add token-level heatmaps and a p99 latency regression alert tied to the prompt family — we should ship these as part of the renewal SOW.

Next steps: Ben/Vanessa, can you confirm routing (Dedicated pool vs. burst hosted) and give an ops delta for both? If both look feasible, I'll prepare a short slide for Liam and procurement with cost deltas and rollback rules.

Kimberly
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: 2026-10-05T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: capacity safety pool ask (ops impact)

All — quick ops summary:

Dedicated pool option:
- Pros: predictable latency, straightforward SLA mapping, charges rolled into Dedicated commit.
- Cons: requires commit amendment (short-term tranche addendum) and longer lead time for guaranteed capacity (~72 hours for firm allocation).

Burst-hosted option:
- Pros: near-immediate capacity, bill-as-you-go for short windows, easier to rollback.
- Cons: slightly higher per-hour cost and potential cold-start KV impacts without warm lane.

Hybrid suggestion (what Kimberly suggested above):
- Start Phase 0 and Phase 1 on burst-hosted with autoscale rules and a small warm lane to minimize upfront commit risk. If Phase 2 triggers persist beyond two weeks, convert the burst to a short-term Dedicated tranche (30–90 day addendum) to stabilize cost and performance.

I'll prepare a routing diagram and incremental cost table for both paths.

— Ben
Head, Capacity Operations
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightpath.ai>, Anya Kaur <anya@brightpath.ai>, BrightPath Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:12:00Z
Subject: Consolidated proposal: staged runway + rollback rules (BrightPath renewal)

Liam / team — thank you for the signal and the CSV. Attached is the consolidated plan: redwood_proposed_reserve_v1.pdf and the usage CSV we reviewed. TL;DR of the proposal below.

Proposed approach (executive summary):
- Phase 0 (immediate): +10 GPUs on burst-hosted for 7 days with a 1-GPU warm lane to validate behavior.
- Phase 1 (conditional): if 7-day rolling median utilization > 70%, auto-scale to +30 GPUs (burst-hosted) and expand warm lane to 8 GPUs.
- Phase 2 (escalation): if 3-day sustained peak > 85% and business confirms, convert to a 30-day Dedicated addendum covering +40 GPUs with a 12% hot standby (5 GPUs warm).
- Rollback: staged downsize when the 14-day median < 55% (50% scale down) and full removal if 28-day median < 50%.

Cost and timing in the PDF; Ben included routing tradeoffs. Observability: we'll add token-level heatmaps and p99 latency regression alerts tied to your prompt family before Phase 1.

Requested next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm whether a short 30-day Dedicated addendum is acceptable as a contingency (DocuSign link included)?
2) Liam — can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to confirm the trigger thresholds and acceptable rollback windows?

If you approve, we'll stand up Phase 0 within 4 hours of sign-off and monitor closely.

Thanks,
Sergio
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
